records.title: Suez / Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb
records.summary: The Houthi’s have resumed attacking commercial ships and continue to pose a threat to U.S. assets operating in the area. M/Ts AMZAN and DAISY were reportedly struck by Houthi missiles off the coast of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia on 24 August 2026. From November 2023 to October 2025, there were more than 100 separate Houthi attacks on commercial vessels affecting more than 60 nations. In July 2025, this trend escalated when the Houthis attacked and sank the bulk carriers MAGIC SEAS and ETERNITY C while transiting the Red Sea in the vicinity of Hodeidah, Yemen. Entities claiming to be Yemeni authorities have also attempted to divert commercial vessels operating in these regions from their course. These threats pose both direct and collateral risks to commercial vessels transiting or operating in these areas. Commercial vessels operating in these areas should be vigilant for hazards to navigation caused by vessels being struck by the Houthis and should be aware of all current navigation warnings.

incident.location: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
incident.exposed: Energy, containerized consumer goods, industrial inputs; route-specific U.S. cargo share not measured.
incident.plausible: Diversion around Africa can lengthen voyages, absorb vessel capacity and increase inventory-in-transit and fuel expense.
incident.recovery: Advisory downgrade or withdrawal, sustained safer transits, and documented carrier resumption.
incident.nature: 2026-013-Red Sea, Bab el Mandeb Strait, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea, and Somali Basin-Houthi Attacks on Commercial Vessels
incident.observed: Active U.S. government maritime security advisory; the source reports threats or incidents. Quantified U.S. throughput loss and delay are not established by this advisory.
incident.confidence: High confidence in official advisory status; U.S. economic impact is an interpretation.

details.methodology: Matched active advisory index and verified detail page; effective date is not asserted to be the physical start of a disruption.

records.title: Persian Gulf / Strait of Hormuz
records.summary: Iran continues to threaten and conduct strikes on commercial vessels transiting the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz (SoH) and Gulf of Oman. Numerous hazards to navigation and risks of Iranian attacks against commercial shipping remain high in these areas. Prior to the commencement of combat operations in this region, Iranian forces historically utilized small boats and helicopters during boarding operations and have attempted to force commercial vessels into Iran’s territorial sea. Iranian threats to commercial vessels now additionally include direct attacks from missiles, armed unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and armed unmanned surface vessels (USVs). The U.S. government is continually assessing the maritime security situation in the region to identify and differentiate threats and safeguard freedom of navigation, ensure the free flow of commerce, and protect U.S. vessels, personnel, and interests.

incident.location: Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman
incident.exposed: Crude oil, refined fuels and LNG; U.S. exposure also runs through globally priced energy.
incident.plausible: Navigation constraints and vessel attacks can tighten energy supply and raise insurance, fuel and transport costs.
incident.recovery: Official threat reduction, sustained transit restoration, and verifiable normalization of cargo flows.

records.title: Black Sea / Sea of Azov shipping
records.summary: Since February 2022, and as recently as September 2026, commercial vessels have reportedly been struck by projectiles and experienced explosions in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. Vessels have also reportedly been struck by drones and unmanned vehicles. Additionally, there have been reports of moored and drifting naval mines. While some past actions may have targeted specific commercial vessels due to their association with certain countries or their activity, the potential remains for miscalculation, misidentification, or accidental strikes caused by electronic warfare (EW) interference with missile and drone guidance systems, resulting in a high risk of damage to commercial vessels in the region. 3. Guidance : U.S.-flagged commercial vessels operating in these waters are advised to exercise caution; conduct a risk assessment; review security measures; review current NATO Shipping Centre, NAVAREA III, and other coastal broadcast warnings; and incorporate appropriate protective measures
